intro.title: Model API success error via discriminated unions
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple function that simulates fetching data from an API and returns a result that is either a success with data or an error with a message. You will learn to model these two possible outcomes using a TypeScript discriminated union, which is a type that can be one of several distinct shapes, each identified by a common property (like 'status'). This approach helps make your code more predictable and type-safe by clearly defining success and error states. You'll work with TypeScript interfaces, union types, and type narrowing to handle each case correctly. By the end, you'll understand how to represent and work with API responses in a robust, typed manner.
intro.usecase: In modern web applications, handling API responses robustly is critical for user experience. For example, a dashboard fetching user data must clearly differentiate between a successful load (displaying charts), a network error (showing a retry button), and an empty state (suggesting initial setup). Using discriminated unions in TypeScript allows developers to model these distinct outcomes with type safety, ensuring the UI correctly renders loading spinners, success content, or error messages without runtime surprises. This pattern is essential in forms, data tables, and any component that interacts with backend services.
